transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Hi. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... yeah, so, I guess what finally made me come in is... well, it's probably not a huge deal, but I've been noticing these little slip-ups lately. 

I'm doing a lot of applications and writing up research notes right now, and I just keep turning them in with these small, kind of embarrassing mistakes? Like, I'll mislabel an artwork date, or I'll just completely skip a question on a form. And I feel really silly about it because I honestly thought I had checked them over really carefully before submitting them. 

I know everyone makes typos sometimes, so I hope I'm not overreacting or wasting your time by being here, but it's just been happening a bit too often. Does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you're asking about?
Have you noticed this kind of difficulty with attention and small mistakes since you were a child, or is this something that's only started recently?

Um, well, I guess... I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I was a bad student or anything, because I really did try hard. But, yeah, I suppose it's been happening for a while. 

Even back in elementary school, my teachers would usually say really nice things about me, like that I had good ideas and was a sweet kid. But they'd also write on my report cards that I'd, you know, forget to turn in a worksheet or lose the instructions for a project. Or I'd miss little details on assignments. My parents actually had to check my backpack pretty much every night to make sure I wasn't missing anything important. 

But I always thought that was just normal kid stuff, you know? Like, most kids are a little disorganized, right? I hope that answers your question... I just don't want to make it seem worse than it actually was.
Aside from these mistakes, have you been feeling excessively worried or on edge about many different things—work, health, relationships—more days than not over the past several months?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I get a little stressed sometimes when I have a big deadline coming up or if I realize I made one of those mistakes, but I think that's pretty normal, right? 

I definitely wouldn't say I'm, like, on edge all the time or worrying about everything. I actually try really hard to stay positive and keep things in perspective. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around worrying all day, because I'm honestly doing okay in that department. Is it alright that I don't feel that way? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed feeling down, sad, or losing interest or pleasure in things you normally enjoy?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I have my moments where I'm a little tired or frustrated if I've been staring at a screen all day, but I don't feel depressed or anything like that. I still really love working on my art and going to museums and hanging out with my friends. 

I'm generally a pretty happy person, honestly. I try to focus on the good things, you know? I hope that's okay to say... I just want to make sure I'm not giving you the wrong idea. Does that make sense?
